title: Photoacoustic Cystography
protocol: Configure the Q-switched Nd:YAG laser (SLII-10; Continuum) to operate at 532 nm.
Tune the wavelength-tunable laser (Surelite OPO PLUS; Continuum) within a range of 680 to 2,500 nm based on the optical absorption peak of the contrast agent.
Set the pulse duration of each laser shot to ~5 nsec and the repetition rate to 10 Hz for optimal performance.
Select an optical wavelength of 667 nm when methylene blue serves as the contrast agent, where its peak absorption occurs.
Generate tunable localized surface plasmon resonance at the NIR spectral region for plasmonic gold nanostructures based on their physical and chemical properties.
Choose a wide range of wavelengths for single walled carbon nanotubes based on their broad absorption spectrum.
Deliver light from the tunable laser to a spherical conical lens through right angle prisms (PS908, Thorlabs).
Generate a donut-shaped light beam pattern after the light passes through the spherical conical lens.
Construct the home-made conical lens using a BK7 lens with a cone angle of 152° and a diameter of 2.5 cm for precise light beam formation.
Redirect the diverging donut-shaped light beam via an optical condenser.
Form a ring-shaped light beam with a dark center on the tissue surface.
Place small animals under a water container for acoustic coupling.
Wrap the bottom opening of the water container with clear thin polyethylene film.
Detect PA waves using a spherically focused ultrasound transducer mounted in the middle of the optical condenser.
Amplify detected PA waves by a broadband ultrasonic pulser/receiver.
Acquire amplified PA waves using an oscilloscope.
Obtain one-dimensional time-resolved images by measuring the times of arrival of PA waves.
Assume the speed of PA waves to be 1,480 m/sec for image acquisition.
Acquire two-dimensional PA images by mechanically moving the linear raster scanning stage along the x and y directions.
Acquire three-dimensional PA images by acquiring data along the z direction with a 50-MHz sampling rate.
Control mechanical scanning using a home-made NI LabVIEW software system.
Represent volumetric data by maximum amplitude projection (MAP) using MathWorks MATLAB software system.
Ensure that the beam pattern after the spherical conical lens is a perfect ring shape.
Align the line-shaped light focus in water coaxially with the ultrasound focal zone.
Use female Spraque-Dawley rats weighing between 200 - 250 g for PA imaging experiments.
Anesthetize the rat by intraperitoneal injection of a mixture of ketamine (85 mg/kg) and xylazine (15 mg/kg).
Depilate the hairs in the abdominal area of the anesthetized rat.
Position the rat atop a custom-made animal holder.
Lubricate a 22-gauge catheter to improve insertion.
Insert the distal end of the lubricated catheter horizontally into the urethra until the hub reaches the opening.
Apply ultrasound gel between the animal skin surface and plastic membrane for acoustic coupling.
Fully anesthetize the rat using vaporized isoflurane (1 L/min of oxygen and 0.75% isoflurane) during PA imaging experiments.
Obtain a control PA image prior to injection of contrast agents.
Introduce an aqueous solution of methylene blue (0.8 μl/g body weight with a concentration of 30 mM) to the bladder via catheter using a 1-ml syringe and a 22-gauge catheter.
Introduce an aqueous solution of gold nanocages (1.2 μl/g body weight with a concentration of 2 nM) to the bladder via catheter using a 1-ml syringe and a 22-gauge catheter.
Introduce an aqueous solution of single-walled carbon nanotubes (0.8 μl/g body weight with a concentration of 0.3 μM) to the bladder via catheter using a 1-ml syringe and a 22-gauge catheter.
Acquire a series of PA images after injection.
Sacrifice the rat by injecting an overdose of pentobarbital after in vivo PAC imaging.
Remove the bladders and kidneys from the sacrificed rat.
Position the excised organs on a glass plate below the water container in the PAC system.
Apply ultrasound gel between the excised organs and plastic membrane to improve acoustic coupling.
Acquire PA images of the excised organs.
Photoacoustically image organs removed from a healthy rat as a control.
